candidate: BrowserWindow with native WebContentsView; Playwright connectOverCDP
scope: Disposable browser-mechanics probe outside the application workspace; no provider keys or existing project data used.

observations.name: displayed-target-identity
observations.evidence: CDP target type page mapped through webContents.fromDevToolsTargetId to guest WebContents ID 2; the view displayed that same WebContents.

evidence.prior_runs: Included hidden document state and normal-click actionability timeouts before the throttling adjustment.

observations.name: background-throttling-disabled
observations.limit: No physical display capture, DPI matrix, or long-running resource benchmark was performed.

observations.name: playwright-native-dom-roundtrip
observations.evidence: Playwright-filled input and sessionStorage nonce matched independent reads from the displayed WebContents; actual click counter was 1.

observations.name: guest-node-isolation
observations.limit: This is not a full sandbox or IPC penetration test.

observations.name: playwright-context-cookie-fidelity
observations.consequence: Do not assume Playwright's returned BrowserContext maps Electron's isolated partition correctly. Session-scoped ancillary APIs need explicit validation/adaptation.

observations.name: playwright-page-route
observations.evidence: page.route aborted a known local diagnostic request; that request did not reach the diagnostic server.

observations.name: blanket-native-input-guard

evidence.guard: before-mouse-event/before-input-event preventDefault while Agent owns control

observations.consequence: A blanket guard vetoes automated clicks too. Physical-user exclusion and trusted CDP input need a separately validated mechanism; a resolved tool call is not proof of the action's effect.

observations.name: escape-destination-reachability
observations.evidence: A separate loopback-only 127.0.0.1 diagnostic destination returned HTTP 200 to the controller before boundary testing.

observations.name: popup-single-audit-page
observations.evidence: window.open was denied; one audit page remained. The trusted UI renderer is separate and is not a second audit browser.

observations.name: user-control-renderer-crash-rebind
observations.limit: Only renderer replacement, target rebinding, and the probe's owner marker were exercised; full Agent scheduling/history reconciliation was not implemented.

observations.name: handoff-pending-renderer-crash-rebind
observations.limit: This does not prove an in-flight operation race, recovery-exhaustion path, or production control handoff.

unvalidated: Physical keyboard, mouse, wheel, IME, drag/drop, accessibility input, and focus exclusion while trusted automation remains functional
Correct partition-scoped cookie/storage/permission/context lifecycle APIs and a constrained production automation transport
Meaningful business-effect permission enforcement in both ownership modes; origins and HTTP methods alone are insufficient
Full Agent/TODO/event-history reconciliation, uncertainty handling, verification, budgets, and secret redaction
Packaged-app hardening and exposure of browser-wide CDP targets
Whole browser-host/main-process failure, as distinct from an audit renderer crash
DPI, resizing, native layering, modal interactions, background execution, and performance coverage
execution_notes: Initial cold binary download exceeded a shell timeout; it was not a browser compatibility result.
Electron's GUI process received EOF on stdin in this launch environment. The probe control channel was corrected to a temporary Windows named pipe before interpreting browser results.
The final probe finished its bounded checks and cleanup. No Electron process remained in the immediate post-run process inspection.

Independent read-only review identified weak boundary-test causality. The final probe added destination reachability, redirect-source, explicit cancellation-event, and no-escaped-request assertions before recording the boundary results.
The prototype's temporary loopback CDP listener is not an approved production security architecture.
Diagnostic failures are preserved. Successful harness execution does not mean all feasibility gates passed.
